title.narrative: Payment system conforms to international norms

actual.value: ATS, APS and CSD systems were installed and functional. It is currently in accordance to the BIS 10 Core Principles for Systemically Important Payments Systems (CPSS) (BIS, 2001):1. The international norms requires: The system should have a well-founded legal basis under all relevant jurisdictions. In this regard the DBA law has given sufficient power to DAB for establishment, maintaining, promoting sound and efficient payment system and participating in it, so DAB has developed and approved the following regulations: Regulation on (DPO) Domestic Payments Operations in Afghanistan (2010) Regulation on (EFT) Electronic Fund Transfers (2015) Regulation on (PSOs) Payment system and payment system operators (2016) Regulation on (EMIs) Electronic Money Institutions (2016) Regulation on (MSPs) Money Service Providers (2016) Regulation on (PSPs) Licensing and Oversight of Payment and Securities Transfer Systems (Payment Service Operator) and Policy framework for (RTGS – ACH) (2018)

title.narrative: Payment system conforms to international norms

actual.value:
ATS, APS and CSD systems were installed and functional. It is currently in accordance to the BIS 10 Core Principles forSystemically Important Payments Systems (CPSS) (BIS, 2001):
1. The international norms requires: The system should have awell-founded legal basis under all relevant jurisdictions. In this regard the DBA law has given sufficient power to DAB forestablishment, maintaining, promoting sound and efficient payment system and participating in it, so DAB has developed and approvedthe following regulations:
Regulation on (DPO) Domestic Payments Operations in Afghanistan (2010) Regulation on (EFT)Electronic Fund Transfers (2015) Regulation on (PSOs) Payment system and payment system operators (2016) Regulation on (EMIs)Electronic Money Institutions (2016) Regulation on (MSPs) Money Service Providers (2016) Regulation on (PSPs) Licensing andOversight of Payment and Securities Transfer Systems (Payment Service Operator) and Policy framework for (RTGS ACH)(2018)
2. Rules and Procedures: The systems rules and procedures should enable participants to have a clear understanding of thesystems impact on each of the financial risks they incur through participation in it. The ATS policy framework (rules andprocedures) has been established and approved by DAB supreme council in 2018 and this is accessible in DAB website. This policyframework delineate basic elements of the system such as unique bank identification codes, user management, membership terms, Queuemanagement, settlement finality, accounting structure, members rights and responsibilities, net settlements, error handling, feesand charges, Claims, Compensation and contingency events and some other information regarding clear understanding of systemfinancial risk.
3. Risk Management: The system should have clearly defined procedures for the management of credit risks andliquidity risks, which specify the respective responsibilities of the system operator and the participants and which provideappropriate incentives to manage and contain those risks. The system does not settle payment transactions if ordering participantDOES NOT have sufficient Balance in its settlement account kept in DABs books. Once the RTGS goes live DAB will only providecollateralized ILF (intraday liquidity Facility) for direct participants of interbank payment systems, therefore the financialrisks (liquidity and credit risks) are zeroed.
4. Settlement Finality: The system should provide prompt final settlement on theday of value, preferably during the day and at a minimum at the end of the day. The RGTS fully supports settlement of transactionsindividually and on real time basis, so the balance of transactions will be posted in settlement accounts of participantsimmediately. (Debit entry to ordering participants account and Credit entry to Receiver participant) and transactions areirrevocable which means once transaction is settled in RTGS cannot be rejected in the system but can be returned in a new and freshpayment transaction by order of beneficiary via receiving banks.
5. Multilateral Netting Takes: A system in which multilateralnetting takes place should, at a minimum, be capable of ensuring the timely completion of daily settlements in the event of aninability to settle by the participant with the largest single settlement obligation. The ACH part of ATS system supportmultilateral netting and in the meanwhile it provides options for the ordering participants to drop any payments not reasonable forsettlement due to any reason. On the other hand DAB will provide collectivized ILF if banks are in shortages of balances in theirsettlement account to discharges its obligations.
6. Assets used for settlement should be a claim on the central bank; where otherassets are used, they should carry little or no credit risk and little or no liquidity risk. Once the payment is settled in RTGSand accounts of parties in RTGS/GL are effected, beneficiary bank can have access to the funds credit

Approval by DAB of financial sector regulations ensuring consistency with international standards

baseline.value: Afghanistan financial sector regulations not fully aligned with international standards

actual.value: A new banking law and AML/CFT regulations were approved. Procurement of TA for Financial Supervision Department (FSD) completed and implementation started in Nov, 2017. The FSD TA suffered some hick ups; however, the activity was concluded in Jan 2020 and the fir provided several deliverables on potential regulatory reforms. This contributed to some regulatory reforms that DAB adopted particularly on CAMELS criteria, accepting partial credit guarantees as collateral. DAB is currently assessing further reforms in view of the TA outcomes. The following regulations were developed and introduced: • Legal Assessment Report against International Standards• Regulation on Licensing and Oversight of Payment and Securities Transfer Systems, and of Money Service Providers• Regulation on Licensing and Oversight of Payment and Securities Transfer Systems• Regulation on Licensing and Oversight of Money Service Provides• DAB General Guidelines on Retail Payments Instruments• Regulation on Elec
